name: Bashar al-Assad
role: President of Syria (2000-2024); in exile in Moscow since December 2024
summary: Ba'ath Party leader who ruled Syria for 24 years. He presented himself as a gradual reformer who opened parts of the economy and promised party and election laws, while resisting Western-style democracy and defending the security response to the 2011 uprising as a fight against a foreign-backed conspiracy and terrorism. Abroad, he demanded the Golan's return, allied with Iran, Hezbollah and Russia and backed Arab unity and a multipolar world.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pulled both ways: he described liberalising the market step by step and opening to private banks (2000-2008), yet said in 2008 the emerging economy was not strong enough to be liberalised fully and in 2019 that Syria stays socialist with a large public sector.

public-ownership.rationale: In 2008 he said liberalisation was proceeding step by step but met more opposition and needed more care for the oil and national sector; in 2019 he said Syria did not follow liberal policy, is still socialist and has a very large public sector. Mixed with his 2000 call to activate the private sector.

state-harmful.rationale: Repeatedly argued for strengthening state institutions and said the state has a duty to meet people's needs and provide services; he treated absence of institutions as the source of chaos and corruption.

decide-locally.rationale: In 2011 he called the local administration law one of the most important reforms, to address problems the present central administration cannot solve.

gradual-change.rationale: Told Syrians to give up uprooting the status quo in totality and to build on what exists, with steady gradual steps (2000); in 2008 said Syria moves slowly and cautiously and cannot move fast.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposed Western military action over Syria, saying a strike would support Al-Qaeda groups and that foreign pretexts of freedom and democracy mask a plot.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said in 2000 that society cannot progress on one party, but kept the Ba'th as the constitutionally leading party until 2012 and allowed no real opposition after; the record wins.

democracy-best.rationale: In 2000 he said Western democracy cannot be copied; in 2008 he said fast political opening risks Algeria-style outcomes and that no sectarian current may be politicised. He also called Syria's system democratic, so the evidence is mixed.

separate-church-state.rationale: Said in 2013 that Syria is secular and fears erosion of the secular state, and kept religion out of politics; the 2012 constitution still required a Muslim president.

civilizational-union.rationale: Called for activating Arab economic conventions and a project of regional unity among Arab states.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said change is a means not an end (2000), that in politics one must be pragmatic and deal with effective players rather than black and white (2008), and that his job is Syria's interests wherever they lie (2019).

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2023 he said Jews who came to Palestine are Khazar converts with no link to the ancient people of Israel; in 2008 he nonetheless negotiated indirectly for a peace treaty with Israel. Mixed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said Syria bases its relations on the right of peoples to self-determination.

dominated-front.rationale: Described ties with Iran, Russia and China and Hamas and Hezbollah as necessary dealing with effective players against what he called Western pressure.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Promised in 2011 that those responsible for killings would be held to account, but no security officials were prosecuted for killing protesters or for detention deaths; the record wins.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Said it is the state's duty to meet people's needs (food, medicine, services, fair distribution of development), which is the opposite of a state limited to defence, justice and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said what is a right for me is a right for others, while his government persecuted opponents and used chemical weapons and barrel bombs on civilians; mixed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Spoke of legitimacy as the people's will, but held power through uncompetitive referendums and elections and met mass protest with lethal force; the record wins.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said the different sectors and colours of Syrian society are members of one body and that the crisis confirmed strong social cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Record: kept the 1963 emergency law until April 2011, then governed through sieges, mass detention and counter-terrorism laws used against protesters; the record wins.

party-controls-media.rationale: Record: the 2001 press law and state ownership kept media under government control and censorship, with brief private openings; the record wins.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Wrote a term limit into the 2012 constitution while restarting the count to stay in office through 2028; mixed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Spoke in 2011 of a constitutional assembly, but the 2012 constitution was drafted by a committee he appointed and put to a referendum under war conditions; the record wins.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said rich Northern countries should shoulder their human responsibilities toward the South.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presided over the 2014 contested presidential election under the 2012 constitution, which he described as the people choosing their president; earlier presidents were confirmed by referendum.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Said peace is Syria's strategic choice but not at the expense of an inch of its territory, and that Israel must return the Golan.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No recorded position. He described the Golan as occupied but did not address annexation without consent.

women-must-cover.rationale: Condemned rebel-held areas where women must be covered head to toe, calling it the Taliban style.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Said Arab states, which share more factors for unity than others, should pursue regional unity.

elective-rulers.rationale: Praised elections as the people's choice, but inherited the presidency from his father and never faced a competitive vote; the record wins.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Made recovery of the Golan, occupied by Israel in 1967, a top national priority and demanded return to the 4 June 1967 line.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said we cannot apply the democracy of others to ourselves and that Syria needs its own democratic experience stemming from its history, culture and needs.

non-intervention.rationale: Insisted on sovereignty and non-interference in Syria's affairs and said the US would violate the UN Charter by striking; Syria's long military presence in Lebanon before 2005 and his invitation of allies are in tension.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said Syria's judicial system and sovereignty would not be replaced by an international tribunal, and any cooperation needs an agreement with the UN.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In a December 2023 speech, as reported by JNS, he said there is no evidence six million Jews were killed and that the issue was politicised to falsify the truth.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Record: ended the Damascus Spring, jailed opposition figures and met the 2011 protests with mass arrests, torture and lethal force, which he defended as fighting terrorists; the record wins.

social-market-economy.rationale: As Ba'ath secretary he opened the 2005 party congress that moved to a mixed economy balancing market openness with the state's social role in health and education; in 2011 he asked for an economic model giving social equity between rich and poor and city and country.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Described long cooperation and political support from Russia and agreements with Iran, and thanked Russia, Iran and China; he did not stay out of rival blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: No recorded position. His own succession to his father is an action, and he made no statement on hereditary succession.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Said that if Lebanon's protests aim at reform and abolition of its sectarian political system, that is useful for Lebanon.

term-limits.rationale: The 2012 constitution he proposed set two seven-year terms, but the count restarted in 2014 and he ran again in 2014 and 2021; mixed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Repeatedly honoured soldiers and others killed defending Syria as martyrs, in 2011 and 2014.

second-chamber.rationale: In 2008 he named an upper house of parliament as a next step to broaden participation.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Spoke of the Arab nation and of Arab nationalism and solidarity as worth reviving beyond state borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Said abolishing Lebanon's sectarian political system would be good for Lebanon.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said Syria faces a conspiracy whose last stage is for Syria to weaken and disintegrate (2011) and called the war a plot against the homeland (2014).

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Offered amnesty to rebels who surrendered arms, while relying on pro-government militias (shabiha, National Defence Forces) and allied foreign armed groups; the record wins.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said women are half of society and must participate actively and that the ground for their participation should be prepared.

close-ties-china.rationale: Said Syria took a strategic direction toward Asia rather than the US and thanked China in 2014; in 2008 he spoke of India and China's rise.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Said no sectarian current is allowed to be politicised and that Islamic groups may act on religion but not in politics; the 2012 draft constitution banned religious parties.

multipolar-world.rationale: In 2008 he said India and China should help create a balance that the world has lacked since the late 1980s.

notes: Living: Wikipedia records no death; he was overthrown on 8 December 2024 and lives in exile in Moscow. Answers rest on his speeches and interviews (2000-2023 reported speech) and on measures he personally drove (2012 constitution, wartime conduct). Contested points are low confidence. No answers are inferred from party, label or his father.
